subject: ventures/timber-sale-offer-checker
professional: a consulting forester who cruises timber and reviews landowner offers; first checks: are the Doyle / Scribner / International 1/4-inch volumes right against the rule definitions and printed tables, is a per-MBF price applied to volume scaled under the same rule it was quoted in, are the prices stumpage (not delivered-log) prices and where they come from, is a lump-sum offer compared like-for-like with a per-unit one, and can a landowner get the input from a timber cruise (trees by DBH and merchantable logs).

evidence.correctness: Independent script /tmp/claude-0/audit-timber/indep.py (python3, no subject import) from the rule definitions: Doyle (D-4)^2 L/16 and International 1/4-inch as 0.904762*(0.22D^2-0.71D) per 4-ft section with 1/2 in taper. Sample logs: Doyle 18,532 BF / $7,915 (subject 18,532 / $7,915, pass); International 24,482 BF / $10,270 (subject 24,478 / $10,269, rounded coefficients, pass); International 16x16 180.6, 12x16 96.9, 20x16 289.7 vs printed table 180/95/290 (pass); forester break-even f/(1-f) 8% -> 8.70, 10% -> 11.11 (pass); per-MBF $300 Doyle on 10 16x16 logs -> $432 (pass). Scribner formula 0.79D^2-2D-4 vs printed Scribner 16-ft table (auditor's recollection of the standard table, not fetched): +8.6% at 12 in (85.8 vs 79), +7.8% at 14 in, -31% at 6 in (partial, labelled an approximation). The headline output is wrong in kind: the ratio prices International volume with the user's single per-MBF price, which carries no rule. Where stumpage is quoted Doyle, an offer exactly equal to Doyle volume x the user's Doyle price is reported as 66% and flagged low (`node cli.mjs small.csv --offer 5376 --price 'red oak=420'` on 200 12x16 red oak logs: 'The offer is 66% of the value these logs have at your prices', exit 1). The page's own example offer ($7,200 = 91% of the Doyle value) is flagged at 70%.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked: board feet under three rules (works), value at user prices with missing species reported (works), implied $/MBF (works), forester break-even (works), CSV export (toCsv tested), CLI with exit 1 under 75% (works), nothing uploaded (page.test asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon). CLI `--price 'red oak=$420'` printed '$NaN' values with ratio n/a and exit 0 (fixed in this session, see craft). Served copy: `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs timber-sale-offer-checker` reports no placeholder or retired origin. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 25 pass, 0 fail (0.24 s). Tests pin Doyle values and International 16x16 within 3 BF (taper mutant caught). quality_mutate.py: the 75% flag threshold (calc.mjs:115, 0.75 -> 0.6), the Scribner coefficient (calc.mjs:13, 0.79 -> 0.75) and the fair-value basis (calc.mjs:93, intl -> doyle) all SURVIVED; only the International taper mutant (calc.mjs:18) was caught. The verdict-driving lines have no test.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (140 lines), cli.mjs, index.html script, all four test files. Pure, small functions, clear. Defects: cli.mjs:16 turned '$420' or 'abc' prices into NaN and printed '$NaN' with exit 0 (the browser parser strips $ but the CLI did not); `--fee abc` is accepted (check() lets NaN through calc.mjs:84) and silently drops the forester line; mbf is computed from rounded bf (harmless). Fixed the CLI price/fee parsing in this session with a test (scores are pre-fix).
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty and 'no market data' (pass, page.test and index.html). 'Not modelled' list is honest (pass). 'Ratio compares the offer with the International value at your prices, the closest to true volume' (index.html:97, README:24) presents a rule-mismatched comparison as the fair benchmark (fail). README:10 'tell whether a timber offer is in the right range' is not backed given that bias (fail). 'Scribner ... can differ from a scale ticket by a few board feet per log' (index.html:95): 7-9 BF and 8% at 12-14 in, 31% at 6 in (partial). llms.txt github.io link is rewritten at deploy (source-only, not a defect).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a landowner with a logger's lump-sum offer on standing timber. The input is a log tally by small-end DIB and length, which a landowner with standing trees does not have; a cruise reports trees by DBH and number of 16-ft logs, converted with form-class volume tables (e.g. Mesavage-Girard FC78), which the tool does not accept. Price is a single $/MBF per species with no stumpage/delivered distinction and no rule, so a user who types mill log prices or Doyle-quoted state stumpage gets a biased verdict. No grade split, cull or pulpwood/cords. A forester could use it as a log-rule side-by-side; a landowner cannot rely on its flag.
evidence.domain: Log-rule math matches the Doyle and International 1/4-inch definitions and the printed International table; break-even uplift f/(1-f) is right. Departures a forester hits in the first hour: price-per-MBF must be paired with the rule it was quoted under (state stumpage reports in the hardwood Midwest/South are Doyle), and the tool applies it to International volume; stumpage vs delivered-log price not distinguished; no tree-based cruise input; Scribner formula rather than the table (or Scribner Decimal C); no defect/cull deduction; lump-sum vs pay-as-cut risk (who scales, buyer's mill tally) is not discussed beyond converting a per-MBF offer.

defects.what: The headline ratio values International volume at the user's single per-MBF price, which has no rule attached. Stumpage prices are quoted per rule (Doyle across much of the hardwood range), so a like-for-like offer on 12-in logs reads 66% and is flagged 'offer looks low' (CLI exit 1); the page's own example offer, 91% of its Doyle value, is flagged at 70%. Prices need a rule input and value at that rule.

Page and README present the International-at-your-price ratio as the benchmark ('closest to true volume') and promise to 'tell whether a timber offer is in the right range', which the rule-mismatched comparison does not back
No stumpage vs delivered-log distinction: the price field is 'price per MBF' with no guidance that offers are stumpage; a user entering mill prices sees every offer as low
Input is a log tally (small-end DIB, length); a landowner selling standing timber has, at best, a cruise by DBH and number of logs, which needs form-class volume tables the tool lacks
The 75% flag threshold and the fair-value basis that drive the verdict have no test: both mutants survived
Scribner uses the 0.79D^2-2D-4 formula: +8.6% at 12 in, +7.8% at 14 in, -31% at 6 in against the printed table, more than the page's 'a few board feet per log'; untested (mutant survived)
CLI --price 'red oak=$420' became NaN and printed '$NaN' values with exit 0; --fee abc accepted and the forester line silently dropped (check() lets a NaN fee through)

verdict: The log-rule arithmetic is right: an independent script reproduces Doyle exactly and International 1/4-inch to 0.02% (and within 2 BF of the printed 16-ft table), and the forester break-even f/(1-f) and per-MBF conversion check out. The verdict the tool exists to give is not sound: it multiplies International volume by a per-MBF price that has no rule, so where stumpage is quoted Doyle a like-for-like offer on 12-in logs reads 66% and is flagged low, and the page's own example is flagged at 70% while sitting at 91% of its Doyle value. It also has no stumpage-vs-delivered guidance, no tree/cruise input, and tests that let the threshold, the fair-value basis and the Scribner formula change unnoticed (3 of 4 mutants survived). Finished as described, below the bar on correctness, claims, verification and fitness.
